questions: Can you confirm your current medications, particularly any changes to antiplatelet or blood-thinning agents in the past year?
preop_note_claims: Patient's medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia.

Current medications are Atorvastatin 20mg once daily, Metformin 500mg twice daily, and Lisinopril 10mg once daily; Aspirin 75mg once daily was stopped 6 months ago due to gastrointestinal discomfort and has not been resumed.
Patient has a known allergy to penicillin, manifested as a rash.
ASA-PS is 3 due to the presence of controlled but significant comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia).
Airway assessment indicates no anticipated difficulties with endotracheal intubation; plan for general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation is appropriate.
handoff_claims: Patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia, all currently managed with medications except Aspirin which was discontinued.
Intraoperative course expected to be uncomplicated for laparoscopic cholecystectomy; anticipate standard emergence and extubation.
Anticipated issue includes potential for delayed gastric emptying or ileus post-op due to laparoscopic insufflation; monitor for signs of respiratory compromise or abdominal distension.
distractors: History of pneumonia resolved 5 years ago
Remote history of right arm fracture (20 years ago), fully healed
Previous diagnosis of mild iron-deficiency anemia, resolved with dietary changes
